title: Nadella responds to 60,000 voluntary departures: AI is rewriting the way we work; I can't bring myself to say everything stays the same

content_html:
On November 16, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella appeared on The Pragmatic Engineer podcast. When asked whether a voluntary departure program involving about 60,000 people meant using AI to improve efficiency and then cut jobs, he neither confirmed nor denied it. He only admitted candidly that AI is rewriting software development, and that work patterns and team structures will change along with it: “Will everything stay the same? I can’t do that.”

He doesn’t want to trap people in teams that haven’t transformed He acknowledged that not all teams have adapted to AI changes, and he doesn’t want to see employees trapped in teams whose transformation is incomplete—if their growth is limited, they can leave, but he would rather see people transfer internally to more suitable roles. Compensation for systems engineers, infrastructure staff, and AI training researchers is rising sharply, while forward deployed engineers (FDEs) are growing fastest.

The details behind the VEO program The program was officially announced on October 26. It is aimed at employees at level 70 and below in selected teams in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., and India, offering stipends and career support, with no age or tenure requirements. Fortune said about 60,000 people are eligible, and Microsoft expects fewer than 5% to actually accept it. The company stressed that it is not hoping for a mass exodus, but rather “getting the right people into the right roles.”

Writing code gets cheaper; verification gets more valuable Former Microsoft engineer Orosz predicts that Microsoft will next undertake a major organizational restructuring, shifting to AI-native teams as the new template. AI-generated code already accounts for 20% to 30% of Microsoft’s total code. Nadella highlighted the key point: once code generation becomes cheap, verifying correctness actually becomes the harder problem. New graduate hiring will have to wait until internal role restructuring is completed first. He finally admitted that discussions about the singularity and jobs disappearing have already made people in the industry anxious, and Microsoft’s job structure will continue to change.
